note: The hedge thesis needs instruments carried by defaulted Venezuelan sovereign or PDVSA bonds, the Citgo creditor process, OFAC sanctions relief, or heavy-sour crude differentials and Gulf Coast refiners. None of the 80 candidates carries any of these. The closest is E71 (WTI touch ladder, October 2026), but it does not express the mechanism. First, it settles in October, before the Dec 31 head-of-state resolution. Second, a Venezuelan transition changes medium-term heavy-crude supply expectations, not front-month WTI extremes. Third, the ladder's range ($80-$150) shows it is driven by the Gulf and Iran (Kharg Island, Israel-Iran ceasefire), which would swamp any Venezuela signal. E60 (Venezuela de facto leader) is the same country and the same political outcome as the primary, not a different part of the world. Holding E60.2 NO would largely cancel C3 YES, not hedge it. Any claim linking C3 to these instruments would not be one I could defend, so I name no instrument.
